Consult Summary:
- 53-year-old man with one week of new, nonpainful swelling of the left elbow, felt slightly warm and fluctuant.
- Clinical impression: likely olecranon bursitis; blood tests planned and short course of oral NSAID recommended; safety-netting and follow-up arranged.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Left elbow swelling present ~1 week, first noticed in shower.
- Symptoms: visible swelling at tip of left elbow, slightly warm to touch, feels fluid-like; described as "weird" sensation adjacent to swelling; not severely painful; range of motion preserved and patient can move elbow normally.
- Onset/progression: insidious onset ~1 week ago, no known trauma.
- Relevant systems review: no other joint pains reported during this visit; no history of eczema or widespread dry skin.
- Social/functional: desk-based work; runs 2–3 times per week; otherwise mobile and active.
- Examination findings: visible swelling at tip of left elbow; area slightly warmer than adjacent skin; minimal tenderness adjacent to swelling, tip of elbow not markedly tender; overlying skin dry; no overt spreading erythema or signs consistent with acute septic joint per clinician.
- Clinical impression: probable bursitis (olecranon bursitis).
- Differential considerations discussed: gout, inflammatory/rheumatologic cause, infection (septic bursitis/septic arthritis) — infection currently considered unlikely by clinician.

Issue 2:
- No additional problems raised during this consult.

Issue 3:
- No additional problems raised during this consult.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg, twice daily, take after food; stop if heartburn (recommended by clinician).
- Patient reports no regular medications prior to this visit.

Allergies:
- Peanut allergy.
- No known drug allergies reported.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis diagnosed by GP a few years ago.
- No other chronic illnesses reported.

Social History:
- Occupation: primarily desk-based.
- Exercise: runs 2–3 times per week.
- Smoking and alcohol use: not mentioned in the consult.
- Living arrangements: not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No preventative care details (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, bone density, vaccinations, optometry, skin check) documented in this consult.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not documented in the transcript.
- Local exam: visible swelling at tip of left elbow; area slightly warm compared with adjacent skin; minimal tenderness adjacent to swelling; tip of elbow skin dry; preserved range of motion; no spreading redness or signs of acute septic arthritis noted by clinician.

Plan:
- Start ibuprofen 400 mg orally twice daily with food; stop if heartburn develops.
- Arrange blood test forms to be mailed to patient for a full screen including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and tests to assess for gout (exact tests not specified in transcript).
- Patient to have bloods performed at local collection site per instructions in mailed pack.
- Anticipated lab result turnaround ~5–6 days after blood draw (clinician estimate).
- Arrange follow-up after blood tests; follow-up may be phone, video, or face-to-face per patient preference; patient advised to contact if worsening.
- Safety-netting: seek urgent review (phone/video or in-person) if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or redness spreads — may represent infection requiring immediate assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs; exact laboratory tests and orders (specific names/tests not listed); imaging (e.g., elbow x-ray or ultrasound) not discussed; documentation of medication reconciliation beyond patient report; no documentation of renal/GI risk assessment prior to NSAID recommendation.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality: generally clear and audible with occasional filler words; clinical content and recommendations are interpretable.
